stops.note: origin disputed: Romans linked it to aperire 'to open', as buds open, while modern scholars favour an Etruscan form of Aphrodite, Apru
gave Middle English averil, replacing Old English Eastermonað, the month Bede (725) ties to a goddess Eostre
respelled after Latin; Chaucer's Canterbury Tales (c. 1387) opens 'Whan that Aprill with his shoures soote'

current_meaning: the fourth month of the year
